course.title: Solana for Solidity Devs: Ship Four Programs
course.one_line_promise: By the end you can build, test, and deploy a PDA-backed SPL-token vault on Solana devnet, and explain exactly how the account model differs from EVM storage.

audience.prior_model: Strong Solidity/EVM model: contracts, storage variables, mappings, gas, revert.
prerequisites: has shipped at least one Solidity contract

terminal_outcomes.statement: build, test, and deploy a PDA-backed SPL-token vault on devnet with correct signer/owner checks
explain how Solana's account model differs from EVM storage

glossary.def: The unit of state on Solana; programs are stateless and read/write accounts passed in (the analog of EVM storage, but external).
A deterministic program-owned address from seeds + a canonical bump; replaces Solidity mappings for per-key state.
One program calling another (e.g. the Token Program); the EVM analog of an external contract call.

brief.title: Your Solidity instincts, mapped onto Solana

objectives.statement: build and deploy a hello-world program and name its EVM equivalents

brief.hook: You can read Solidity in your sleep. Most of that intuition transfers to Solana — until it suddenly, expensively doesn't. Let's get a program deployed and find the seams.
brief.concept_spec: The 1:1 map: program≈deployed contract, instruction≈function, signer≈msg.sender, compute≈gas. Worked example: deploy hello-world and read the log. One new element: the build/deploy/invoke loop.
brief.artifact_spec: Build and deploy hello-world to a local validator; invoke it; see the greeting in the logs.
brief.exercise_spec: Completion: change the logged message (TODO) and redeploy. Solo: add a second instruction. Accept: both messages appear in the logs.
brief.the_tradeoff: Leading with EVM mappings gets you productive fast, BUT a few of those mappings are traps — the account model (next modules) is where the analogy breaks.

footguns: assuming a contract holds its own state

brief.assessment: deploy hello-world and show a changed log line
brief.voice_notes: course opener; spine carries it; the 'until it expensively doesn't' line is the hook.

brief.title: Where gas and revert went

objectives.statement: explain how compute units replace gas and how program errors replace revert
set a compute budget and return a custom error

brief.hook: In Solidity, gas and require() were always in your hands. On Solana they're still here — renamed, repriced, and with sharper edges. Where did they go?
brief.concept_spec: Compute units ≈ gas (a per-transaction budget you can raise); custom program errors ≈ revert reasons. Worked example: add a compute-budget instruction and a custom error to hello-world. One new element: the compute budget.
brief.artifact_spec: Augment the program with a compute-budget request and an instruction that returns a custom error on bad input.
brief.exercise_spec: Completion: raise the compute unit limit (TODO). Solo: add a second error variant. Accept: the error surfaces by name in the test.
brief.the_tradeoff: A raisable compute budget is flexible, BUT every unit costs priority fee — and unlike gas, you set the limit up front, so under-budgeting fails the whole transaction.

footguns: swallowing errors instead of returning typed ones

brief.assessment: anchor test: the custom error is returned on bad input; the tx fits the set budget
brief.voice_notes: map-from-known framing; derive WHY the budget is up-front, not metered as you go.

brief.title: Where state lives: accounts, not storage variables

objectives.statement: explain why Solana programs are stateless and where their state lives
create and write to a data account from a program

brief.hook: In Solidity, `uint public count;` just... persists. You wrote to storage and forgot about it. Your first Solana program has nowhere to put `count`. Where did storage go?
brief.concept_spec: Programs are stateless code; state lives in separate accounts the caller passes in. Teach by building a counter whose value lives in a data account. One new element: the data account (defer PDAs to next lesson).
brief.artifact_spec: A counter program with an initialize and increment; the count stored in a plain data account.
brief.exercise_spec: Completion: fill in the account's space/size (TODO). Solo: add a decrement. Accept: value persists across two separate transactions; test passes.
brief.the_tradeoff: Separating code from state buys Solana parallelism (txs touching different accounts run concurrently) — BUT you must pass every account a program will touch, and size/rent it yourself up front.

footguns: forgetting the account is not auto-created

brief.assessment: anchor test: increment persists across txs; reading back returns the new value
brief.fading: fully worked counter shown; completion problem for sizing; solo for decrement
brief.voice_notes: contested 'why is it built this way' — Vitalik craft over the spine; the parallelism payoff is a great order-of-magnitude seam. Map from Solidity storage explicitly.

brief.title: Per-user state with a PDA (the mapping you don't have)

objectives.statement: explain why Solana has no mappings and how PDAs replace them
derive a canonical PDA seeded by the user and store per-user state under it

brief.hook: In Solidity you'd write mapping(address => Vault). Solana has no mappings. So how does each user get their own vault?
brief.concept_spec: PDAs: program-owned, deterministically-derived accounts (seeds + canonical bump). Build it twice — native find_program_address, then the Anchor seeds/bump constraint — so the abstraction is visible. One new element: the PDA derivation.
brief.artifact_spec: Upgrade the counter into a per-user vault PDA, seeded by the user's pubkey, with initialize and a balance.
brief.exercise_spec: Completion: fill in the seeds array (TODO). Solo: add a second PDA keyed by a label. Accept: two users get distinct, recoverable vaults; a reinit attempt fails.
brief.the_tradeoff: PDAs are deterministic and need no stored key, BUT you must store or recompute the canonical bump, and a sloppy seed scheme is an exploit (collision / spoofing).
brief.assessment: anchor test: two users get distinct vaults; reinit attempt fails
brief.voice_notes: build-it-twice guest: show native then Anchor; the 'mapping you don't have' framing is the seam.

brief.title: Deposit an SPL token: your first CPI

objectives.statement: transfer SPL tokens into a program-controlled account via a CPI

brief.hook: Your vault holds SOL. Real protocols hold tokens. To move a user's USDC, your program has to call another program — the Token Program. How does one program call another?
brief.concept_spec: Cross-Program Invocation: invoke / invoke_signed; the vault PDA signs for itself. One new element: the CPI (token mechanics introduced alongside).
brief.artifact_spec: Add a deposit_token instruction that CPIs into the Token Program to move tokens from the user's ATA into the vault's ATA.
brief.exercise_spec: Completion: fill the CPI accounts struct (TODO). Solo: add withdraw_token with an owner check. Accept: deposit moves the balance; unauthorized withdraw fails.
brief.the_tradeoff: CPIs make programs composable (your vault works with any SPL token) — BUT each adds compute cost and a trust surface; signing as a PDA means the seeds must match exactly or the CPI fails.
brief.assessment: anchor test: token balance moves on deposit; withdraw by non-owner reverts
brief.fading: CPI accounts shown once; completion problem for the struct; solo for withdraw
brief.voice_notes: documented mechanism → Helius expository craft; flag security footguns inline (Footguns dose, not a full epoch).

brief.title: Ship your own program

objectives.statement: design, build, test, and deploy an original program using a PDA + an SPL-token CPI

brief.hook: You've shipped the pieces. Now build something that's yours — small, real, and on devnet by the end of the day.
brief.concept_spec: Integration: combine account state, a PDA, and a token CPI into one original program of the learner's choosing. No new primitive — this consolidates everything.
brief.artifact_spec: An original small program (learner's design) using an account/PDA + an SPL-token CPI, deployed to devnet with a passing test suite.
brief.exercise_spec: Solo: design and ship it. Accept: deploys to devnet; tests pass; signer + owner checks on every mutating instruction.
brief.the_tradeoff: Freeform scope is motivating, BUT it's where untested edge cases hide — the test suite is the gate, not the demo.

footguns: skipping owner checks under time pressure

brief.assessment: deployed devnet program id + passing test suite (signer/owner checks present)
brief.voice_notes: course close; spine carries it; celebrate the ship, name the one trade-off they chose.

assessment.gate_principle: Completion is gated on a deployed program + passing tests, never on watching.

proof_matrix.evidence: deployed devnet program id + passing test suite

checkpoints.spec: Explain where state lives and why programs are stateless; name one trade-off vs EVM storage.

cumulative_checkpoint.spec: PDA vault that deposits an SPL token via CPI with an owner check, reusing account validation from every prior build.

capstone.statement: Ship an original small program using a PDA + an SPL-token CPI, deployed to devnet, with passing tests.
rubric: uses a PDA with the canonical bump stored
